title: Investigation of the Role of the Orexin System in Mediating Alcohol Cue-induced Nucleus Accumbens Response Using Dual Receptor Antagonistic Modulation and Functional Magnetic Response Imaging (fMRI)
summary: The brain's orexin system and its receptors have been identified as key players in regulating the response to alcohol-related cues. Animal studies have shown that substances which reduce activity in the orexin system can partly reverse heightened reactivity to alcohol cues and increased alcohol consumption in test animals. These findings suggest that, in humans as well, modulating the orexin system might lead to a reduced response to alcohol cues and decreased activity in the brain’s reward system. As this has not yet been studied in humans, the current study aims to investigate how modulating the orexin system affects brain activation in individuals with alcohol use disorder when they are exposed to alcohol-related cues. To do this, half of the participants will be randomly assigned to receive the so-called orexin receptor antagonist Daridorexant (Quviviq, Idorsia®) in tablet form. These participants will be compared to the other half, who will  receive a placebo (a "dummy" pill without an active ingredient). The results of this study may provide important insights into the role of the orexin system in regulating alcohol consumption and help to identify new treatment options for alcohol use disorder.

interventions.name:
Arm 1: Intervention group: 
Combined stress and alcohol cue exposure followed by the assessment of neural alcohol cue-reactivity using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) after antagonistic modulation of the orexin system through administration of Daridorexant (Quviviq, Idorsia®, 50 mg) at

Arm 2: Placebo group: 
Combined stress and alcohol cue exposure followed by the assessment of neural alcohol cue-reactivity using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) after antagonistic modulation of the orexin system through administration of placebo at a single time point.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Individuals with insomnia > 3 months according to the ICD-10 (i.e. indication for receiving daridorexant as part of clinical routine practice) and that use alcohol regularly and meet definition of the research diagnosis of an alcohol use disorder (AUD) according to DSM-5 (i.e. that meet 2 or more DSM-5 criteria of AUD). 

Participants will be screened and enrolled during routine clinical treatment at the Central Institute of Mental Health (independent of study). 

Inclusion Criteria 
- Age between 18 and 65 years 
- Participants diagnosed with insomnia according 
to the ICD-10 
- Regular alcohol use (>2/week & >=2 of 11 criteria 
of an alcohol use disorder according to DSM-5) 
- Ability of the individual to understand the character and the individual consequences of the study 
- Written informed consent (must be available 
before enrollment in the study) 
- Consent to random assignment
Exclusion criteria:
- Current psychotic or bipolar disorder or current severe depressive episode with suicidal ideations 
- Contraindication for functional magnetic 
resonance imaging (e.g. metal implants) 
- Pregnancy, lactation or breastfeeding 
- Current severe somatic comorbidities: liver 
cirrhosis, severe liver dysfunction (Child Pugh Score: ≥ 7) or severely impaired renal function, severe heart insufficiency, pre-existing epilepsy, narcolepsy 
- History of hypersensitivity to Daridorexant (Idorsia®) or to any drug with similar chemical structure or to any excipient present in the pharmaceutical form of Daridorexant (Idorsia®) 
- Any withdrawal symptoms at the time of the study visit (CIWA score >3) 
- Breath alcohol concentration > 0.0 at the time of the study visit 
- Positive drug screening (amphetamines/ecstasy, opiates, cocaine, barbiturates, cannabis, benzodiazepines) 
- Current treatment with daridorexant or other orexin receptor antagonists or use of these drugs within the last 7 days 
- Simultaneous use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. erythromycin, ciprofloxacin, cyclosporine) 
- Acute suicidal tendency or acute endangerment of self and others
